general_concepts.definition: A process in **dialogical movement** from the present, given reality towards the person's goals and intentions[cite: 209].
general_concepts.expression: An expression of the (mostly unconscious) human intention to **be-come**, to come into existence[cite: 210].

general_concepts.focus: An **interpersonal paradigm** (a complement and counterweight to the individualistic paradigm of freedom and personal will)[cite: 275].
general_concepts.core_activity: The most original activity of personhood: Our being essentially **dialogical**, prone to and directed towards **exchange with others**[cite: 277].

general_concepts.definition: Human existence is based on these four fundamental realities, which are the **foundation of a fulfilled life**[cite: 1176, 1228].
general_concepts.function: They form a **matrix for the psychopathological understanding** of psychological disorders and represent the **structure model for modern Existential Analytical Psychotherapy**[cite: 218, 1180].

motivational_process_pea.core_action: Motivation means **involvement of the person**, initiating the personal processes by **provocation in some kind of vis-à-vis**[cite: 292].
motivational_process_pea.starting_point: Being provoked means **being called**[cite: 291]. [cite_start]The necessary provocation comes through everything which **confronts us, challenges us, engages us**[cite: 290].

steps.description: **Recognizing something in its worth or value, in as far as it speaks to...**[cite: 295].

primary_domains.theme_name: The ability to be; to endure/uphold. (FM of World/Reality)
primary_domains.justification_quote: The following table: "Noetic content: 1. TRUE (reality)" and "Motivation: Will to be" and "Mode of experience: can" [cite: 1]
primary_domains.task_as_cornerstone: First come to terms with his or her **being in the world**[cite: 215].

sub_themes.justification_quote: Noetic content: 1. TRUE (reality) [cite: 1]
This demands three things: protection, space and support. [cite: 2]
My active part in this fundamental condition of being there is to accept the positive sides and to endure the negative ones. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Fundamental Trust, Confidence in Self, Faith [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: The sum of these experiences of trust is the fundamental trust, the trust in whatever I feel as being the last support in my life. [cite: 2]
If this is not the case, the result will be restlessness, insecurity and fear. [cite: 2]
Each fundamental motivation has four types of coping reactions: the basic reaction type - here this would be avoidance or flight [cite: 2]
the paradoxical reaction type or activism - here this would be overactivity like fighting bacteria by compulsive washing [cite: 2]
the third type of coping reaction is a specific aggression...- here it would be a destructive aggression such as hate [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Denial or Pretending to be Non-Existent [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: the last type of coping reaction is a reflex of freezing, of death imitation with paralysis - here denial or pretending to be non-existent. [cite: 2]

primary_domains.theme_name: The ability to feel value/life. (FM of Life/Value)
primary_domains.existential_question: I am alive - do I like this fact? [cite_start]Is it good to be there? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_question_quote: I am alive - do I like this fact? [cite_start]Is it good to be there? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_quote: The following table: "Noetic content: 2. ATTRACTIVE (value)" and "Motivation: Will to value" and "Mode of experience: like" [cite: 1]
primary_domains.task_as_cornerstone: Then with **his or her own life**[cite: 215].

sub_themes.justification_quote: Noetic content: 2. ATTRACTIVE (value) [cite: 1]
In order to seize my life, to love it, I need three things: relationship, time and closeness. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Seizing Life / Consent to Being Touched [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: If life is to make me move freely, my consent to being touched is necessary. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Fundamental Value, Harmony, Sense of Depth of Life [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: These experiences form the fundamental value, the most profound feeling for the value of life. [cite: 2]
If relationships, closeness and time are lacking, longing will arise, then coldness and finally depression. [cite: 2]
The basic coping reaction on this level is regression. [cite: 2]
The activism here is overprotection or achievement, typical forms of combating evil [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Fury or Rage (to obtain or improve relationship) [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: the typical aggression is fury, rage which does not lead to destruction, but wants to agitate the other person with the impulse to obtain or to improve the relationship. [cite: 2]
Resignation reaction of feigned death paralyzed half-way. [cite: 2]

primary_domains.theme_name: The ability to be oneself; to be just. (FM of Self/Justice)
primary_domains.existential_question: I am myself - may I be like this? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_question_quote: I am myself - may I be like this? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_quote: The following table: "Noetic content: 3. RIGHT (relations)" and "Motivation: Will to the right" and "Mode of experience: may" [cite: 1]
primary_domains.task_as_cornerstone: And finally with **his or her identity**[cite: 215].

sub_themes.justification_quote: Noetic content: 3. RIGHT (relations) [cite: 1]
In order to succeed here, it is necessary to have experienced three things: attention, justice and appreciation. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Saying 'Yes to myself' through Encounter and Regret (Delimitation) [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: I also have to say "yes to myself". This requires again my active participation: to look at other people, to encounter them and, at the same time, to delimitate myself and to stand by my own, but to refuse whatever does not correspond to myself. [cite_start]Encounter and regret are the two means by which we can live our authenticity without ending up in solitude. [cite: 2]
The sum of these experiences builds one's own worth, the profoundest worth of what identifies my own self at its core: the self-esteem. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Solitude, Hysteria, Need to Hide behind Shame, Loneliness [cite: 2, 1231]
sub_themes.justification_quote: If these experiences are missing, solitude will be the result, hysteria as well as a need to hide behind the shame. [cite: 2]
The coping reactions of this motivation are: distancing oneself as the basic reaction [cite: 2]
stubborn insistence and leading a functional life as form of activism. [cite: 2]
The typical aggressive reaction consists in indignation, annoyance anger, reproach. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Dissociation (of bodily integrity), Dividing and Splitting (of emotion and cognition) [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: The freezing type of reaction at this level are dissociation of the bodily integrity, dividing and splitting of emotion and cognition. [cite: 2]

primary_domains.theme_name: The ability to do good; to be creative/meaning. (FM of Meaning/Future)
primary_domains.existential_question: I am there - for what is it good? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_question_quote: I am there - for what is it good? [cite: 2]
primary_domains.justification_quote: The following table: "Noetic content: 4. MEANING" and "Motivation: Will to act/Will to meaning" and "Mode of experience: should/want" [cite: 1]
primary_domains.task_as_cornerstone: Subsequent to these tasks, the person is open for and prone to **enter into relationships with a greater context (horizon), from which personal meaning is derived**[cite: 216].

sub_themes.justification_quote: Noetic content: 4. MEANING (commitment) [cite: 1]

sub_themes.concept: A Field of Activity, A Structural Context, A Value to be Realized in the Future [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: For this three things are needed: a field of activity, a structural context and a value to be realized in the future. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: The Most Valuable, Realistic Possibility in the Given Situation [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: We define meaning as "the most valuable, realistic possibility of the given situation, for which I feel I should decide myself". [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Bringing Self into Correspondence with the Situation (Phenomenological Attitude) [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: My active part in this attitude of openness is to bring myself into correspondence with the situation, to examine whether what I am doing is really a good thing: for others, for myself, for the future, for my environment. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Sense of Fulfillment, Dedication, Action, Religious Belief [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: The sum of these experiences add up to the meaning of life and leads to a sense of fulfillment. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Feeling of Emptiness, Frustration, Despair, Addiction, Absurdity [cite: 2, 1231]
sub_themes.justification_quote: If this is not the case, the result will be a feeling of emptiness, frustration, even despair and frequently addiction. [cite: 2]

If man fails systematically to reach meaning, his coping reactions will be a provisional attitude towards life as basic reaction, together with a 'planless, day-to-day attitude toward life' and 'collective thinking' (Frankl 1973, XVI) [cite: 2]
idealisation and fanaticism as main forms of activism [cite: 2]
aggressive games and cynicism. [cite: 2]

sub_themes.concept: Fatalism, Loss of Interest, Apathy, Nihilism [cite: 2]
sub_themes.justification_quote: Fatalism (Frankl 1973, XVI), loss of interest, apathy and probably nihilism can be seen as forms of freezing reactions. [cite: 2]
